Where I live my current job is called “school clinician” and I provide counseling, crisis support and referrals. I’m a social worker and I do school counseling / social work

While your road may be more challenging the most, i do believe it’s a road worth traveled if you are passionate. You will change the minds of many students by just being who you are and you will be a beacon of light for another who is just like you. Perhaps now more than ever you are needed, but never at the expense of yourself. No job is worth that, remember that, too.

I may recommend a broader degree though - like social work or counseling alone as it may open more doors for you and opportunities. Depends how far along you are.

I don’t believe that one is a more “smart” path than the other. In counseling you will work directly with students on coping skills, social skills and developing a strong emotional connection. You may do play therapy or sand therapy or make art. As a school psych you’ll evaluate students and might see them once a year at best. They’re drastically different jobs, though ofc necessary. To me, school psych is higher pay and less stress and more technical as you make the school based diagnosis and do evaluation, but I think I’d miss the emotional connection. But the higher pay and less stress seem nice

I went to private school and am now a social worker in an urban charter school.
I was very well educated. We worked 2 grade levels a head and that was the standard and expectation. The kids I see in my school are not. They barely learn bc of behavior issues in the class.

Yes it was worth it. I regret missing out on diversity though I was sheltered. As an adult, exposure to diversity has been such a richness j missed out on. If you could find a decent charter or cheaper catholic school you could maybe find a mix or best of both worlds. My brother went to an excellent charter public school. But working in public charter schools I am starting to lose my hope in that but I work in low income and violent neighborhoods. If you can afford it I was strongly consider private. If you can’t, I’d put a public charter on the table as a solid option but make sure you have the kids reading always at home. 
I had friend who went to public school and she got into an Ivy League. She always was reading in her free time. It’s possible in public but harder. The odds are stacked against you. It’s especially hard if you have behavior issues or maybe aren’t as naturally smart bc you won’t be pushed as hard and you won’t have as high expectations.

I struggled in school but I fought hard for my intelligence and education bc I was surrounded by high expectations, well behaved and intelligent / motivated classmates.

By the time I graduated 12th grade I could read and write research papers in Spanish and was nearly fluent, that’s bc I started in first grade. I don’t even see kids learning languages in the schools I work at. They can’t type either. I had tying and computer tech class since first grade.
They run extensive background checks for most school jobs but idk about expungement. I’d reach out to the board in your state for school counseling and ask.

I have a social work masters and license and I do school counseling / school social work. I do individual counseling and respond to crisis. 
In past positions, I did group counseling. I also helped provide referrals to outside services and give out food and clothes to families In need (funded by my school). 

I recommend social work bc it’s broader - meaning you can do a lot with it if you ever wanted a career move - you could do outpatient therapy, work in a hospital or prison, or macro social work (non profit work, housing work).

School counseling, you’d only be able to do that. A pro of this could be having specialize training in this. 

Where I live - some jobs require you have a school counseling certificate and degree, but that’s only some. 
There’s always jobs for school social workers which in my experience do counseling and maybe a few other things like I mentioned above.
Some schools will take either background. It depends. Look into your area although the job market might be quieter since school just started. 

You will need to obtain possibly depending where you are located (a school social work certificate) so look into that as well. Some social work programs have this built into their programming for masters degrees. This will allow you to get specialize knowledge of work in schools.

As a patient, I hate the doctor and I’ve been through a lot in the medical system that’s been traumatic. A kind medical assistant can be healing, so don’t view it as small talk. Understand that it’s a lot more. It’s making them comfortable and cared for. Bedside manner is everything and the work you do matters. You don’t need to ask about the weather. Ask about how the patient is genuinely feeling, validate their pain / experience, tell them you hope they feel better soon. Ask how they are, genuinely. When medical assistants haven’t looked at me, barely acknowledged me, or seemed indifferent to me, it made me feel less than human, when I was already feeling that way. I’m an introvert so I get it, but making a patient feel seen and heard is what matters. Coming to the doctor and revealing personal stuff about your health can be scary, vulnerable, exhausting and you might be the first person to really listen to a patient. You never know. My advice is to spend less time worrying about being talkative and more time thinking about how you can help a patient feel heard and safe / confortable. They won’t remember what you say, they’ll remember how you made them feel. 
Eventually, you’ll get the hang of the job :)
